suggestions.title: Hand back this morning's five set additions — keep Friday's three

rationale.science: The largest dose-response analysis available (Pelland 2025, 67 studies, 2,058 participants) puts returns per set highest at 5-10 weekly sets and only intermediate at 11-18; >=10 hard sets is the floor, not the target (Schoenfeld 2017). On limited recovery the marginal set costs more than it buys.
rationale.data: Friday you added hams 4-to-6, chest 6-to-8, rear delt 6-to-8 — all three at or under the growth floor by your app's own count. This morning you added five more: quads 10-to-12, abs 10-to-12, biceps 10-to-12, triceps 9-to-11, back 8-to-10. Every one of those climbs out of the 5-10 tier, and it happened 24 hours after you approved the card asking you to stagger two.
rationale.relationship: Your next upper day now carries seven changes at once — press 4th set, rear delt 4th, triceps 4th, biceps 4th, rows 3rd, the press 250 ownership repeat, and the rows hold release — into a recovery state your own app reads WATCH with two unlogged nights behind it. Your app promised each push its own conversion verdict; eight simultaneous changes makes all eight unreadable.

suggestions.predict: Undo today's five (each has a one-tap undo on file) and the next upper day gives you attributable reads on chest and rear delt. Run all seven and I expect at least two 'did not convert' verdicts inside two weeks that neither of us can assign a cause to, plus a press 250 ownership repeat landing on the same day as a fourth press set — which means it cannot bank clean. Grade on the next upper session's entry counts: press 4 / rearDelt 4 / tricep 4 / curl 4 / rows 3 means all seven ran.

suggestions.title: Log Friday and Saturday nights — an unlogged night doesn't flag debt, it hides it

rationale.science: At equal deficits, 5.5 vs 8.5 h sleep cut fat loss about 55% and raised lean-mass loss about 60% (Nedeltcheva 2010; Wang 2018). Sleep is the recovery currency the eight new sets are being charged to.
rationale.data: sleep.nights stops at 8/6 (7.75 h). 8/7 and 8/8 are unlogged. Your 11-night mean is 6.8 h and the 7-night debt is 1.8 h against the 7.5 h you set.
rationale.relationship: The debt flag is a three-night calendar mean (threshold 7.0 h), and when three consecutive nights aren't on file it returns clean. Two dark nights don't make the app cautious, they make it confident — and your next upper day carries the press 250 ownership repeat, which only banks on a genuinely clean day.

suggestions.predict: Log 8/7 and 8/8, and bed by 00:30 tonight for 7.5 h. Grade on sleep.nights gaining entries for 8/7 and 8/8 within 24 hours, and on the next session's lastMeta.debt being computed from three real nights instead of laundered by two missing ones. If both nights get logged and both were 7 h or better, the flag was honest and I will say so.

suggestions.title: Two clean morning reads this week — the food changed and the instrument went dark

rationale.science: A single reading is noise around a slow-moving trend; sodium and carbohydrate move water and scale weight, not fat (Juraschek 2020; Powers 2003). Down-weight the reading, don't throw it away.
rationale.data: 8/7 no read. 8/8 evening only — your app marked it offWindow and set it aside. 8/9 came in at 164.5 the morning after Saturday's high-sodium day. Your measured water sensitivity is +1.11 lb after a salted day, and trend 163.37 + 1.11 is 164.5 — today's read is water to the ounce, not information. One usable morning read in three days.
rationale.relationship: Your intake has run about 2,875 for four days against a measured maintenance of roughly 2,850-3,050 — a deficit near zero. The 14-day rate still says 0.97 lb/wk because half that window predates the change. A run of clean morning reads is the only instrument that can show whether the trend actually flattened.

suggestions.predict: Two in-window morning reads on 8/10 and 8/11. As the salt clears I would expect 162.8-163.4 — priced at the optimistic edge of my range on purpose, because my weight forecasts have run about 2 lb pessimistic three times running. If they come in at 163.5 or above on clean mornings, that is the four maintenance days showing up and I will call the trend flat. Grade on reads gaining 8/10 and 8/11 with no offWindow flag.
